video_caption: A male speaker in a red polo shirt with a striped collar is visible in the bottom right corner, sitting in front of a light yellow and green floral tapestry. The main screen displays a presentation slide with a light grey background featuring a white circuit board pattern. A large dark grey rectangular box in the center of the slide initially shows the title: "Deep Learning Applications: AI in Banking," with a red underline appearing beneath "AI in Banking" at the 0:08 mark. In the bottom left corner, a blue rectangle contains the text "Digital Science Center." At 0:21, the slide transitions, and the text in the dark grey box changes to "AI in Banking" at the top, followed by "A: The Transition of legacy Banks." A red underline then appears under "A: The Transition of legacy Banks" and extends to encircle the phrase "legacy Banks" by 0:29. The speaker continues to gesture with his hands as he talks. At 0:47, the slide changes again to a new design. The left side now displays "Types of AI Applications in Banking" as a title, with "Business Insider Intelligence Jun. 17 2020" below it. The right side features a bar chart titled "Investment Banks And Insurers Using AI Applications, By Type," showing data for "Natural language processing," "Image analysis," "Robotic process automation," "Predictive analysis," and "Machine learning" for both "Investment banks" (dark blue bars) and "Insurance companies" (black bars), with percentages indicated above each bar. A detailed source description is provided below the chart. The speaker is still visible in the bottom left corner, looking towards the presentation slide.

The video displays an older man with light skin, short brown hair, and glasses, wearing a dark blue shirt, speaking from the bottom-left corner. He is gesturing with his hands while looking towards the camera. On the left side of the screen, a white slide with black text reads "Types of AI Applications in Banking" with "Business Insider Intelligence Jun. 17 2020" beneath it, and "Digital Science Center" at the bottom-left. On the right side, a bar chart is displayed with the title "Investment Banks And Insurers Using AI Applications, By Type" and the subtitle "Select global markets." The chart shows five categories on the X-axis: "Natural language processing," "Image analysis," "Robotic process automation," "Predictive analysis," and "Machine learning." For each category, two bars represent "Investment banks" (dark blue) and "Insurance companies" (lighter blue/grey), with corresponding percentages shown above each bar. As the man speaks, red circles are drawn to highlight "Natural language processing," "Image analysis," "Robotic process automation," and then a larger circle encompassing both "Predictive analysis" and "Machine learning." Below the chart, the source is cited: "Source: The Economist Intelligence Unit and Thoughtspot, 'The road ahead: Artificial intelligence and the future of financial services,' June 2, 2020 Methodology: Data is from the June 2, 2020 Economist Intelligence Unit report titled 'The road ahead: Artificial intelligence and the future of financial services,' which was commissioned by Thoughtspot. 200 business executives and C-suite managers performing both IT and non-IT functions at investment and retail banks and insurance companies were surveyed via qualitative and quantitative interviews from February 3-24, 2020. 1012304534636 BUSINESS INSIDER INTELLIGENCE."

The video segment displays a presentation slide titled "UK Bank Closings January 30, 2020," detailing financial news from the United Kingdom. The first bullet point states, "LLOYDS BANKING GROUP ANNOUNCES MORE BRANCH CLOSURES FOR 2020: Lloyds Banking Group plans to close an additional 56 branches this year as part of its continued cost-cutting efforts, per Reuters. The branch closures are expected to happen by October across the banking group's affiliates, including 31 branches at Lloyds, 10 branches at Halifax, and 15 branches at Bank of Scotland. This follows Lloyds' move to shutter 569 branches over the past two years." A red line highlights the phrase "MORE BRANCH CLOSURES" within this text. The second bullet point reads, "There were over 3,300 branch closures in the UK between January 2015 and August 2019 — equivalent to 34% of the overall branch network in the UK. At the same time, nearly 3,000 ATMs closed in the UK in the last six months of 2018, and an additional 1,250 free ATMs started charging fees in the March 2019. The fact that these factors are happening in tandem has led to a cash access crisis in the UK, causing subsequent pushback from regulators and consumer advocates." Red circles are drawn around "3,300" and "3,000 ATMs" in this section. The final bullet point provides a source: "Business Insider Intelligence" with an accompanying URL. In the bottom-right corner, a speaker, a man with short gray hair and glasses, wearing a red polo shirt, is visible in a small rectangular window. He is looking towards the left, presumably at the presentation content, and occasionally makes small gestures with his right hand as he speaks. A "Digital Science Center" logo is visible in the bottom-left corner of the slide.

The video displays a white slide titled "UK Bank Closings January 30, 2020" in large black font, with several bullet points detailing banking trends in the UK. The first bullet point states, "LLOYDS BANKING GROUP ANNOUNCES MORE BRANCH CLOSURES FOR 2020: Lloyds Banking Group plans to close an additional 56 branches this year as part of its continued cost-cutting efforts, per Reuters. The branch closures are expected to happen by October across the banking group's affiliates, including 31 branches at Lloyds, 10 branches at Halifax, and 15 branches at Bank of Scotland. This follows Lloyds' move to shutter 569 branches over the past two years." Key phrases like "MORE BRANCH CLOSURES" and "additional 56" are underlined in red. The second bullet point reads, "There were over 3,300 branch closures in the UK between January 2015 and August 2019 — equivalent to 34% of the overall branch network in the UK. At the same time, nearly 3,000 ATMs closed in the UK in the last six months of 2018, and an additional 1,250 free ATMs started charging fees in the March 2019. The fact that these factors are happening in tandem has led to a cash access crisis in the UK, causing subsequent pushback from regulators and consumer advocates." Numbers like "3,300" and "3,000 ATMs" are also highlighted with red underlines. The third bullet point simply says "Business Insider Intelligence" followed by a web address. In the bottom right corner, a man wearing a red polo shirt is visible, framed against a light yellow background with some abstract art. He is looking towards the left side of the screen, possibly at the slide. A blue banner with the white text "Digital Science Center" is present in the bottom left corner.

From 00:04 to 00:24, a man in a red polo shirt is visible in the top right corner of the screen, speaking and occasionally gesturing with his right hand. The main part of the screen displays a white slide titled "Downsizing Physical Branches". The slide contains bullet points detailing a report from December 4, 2019, about Italy's largest bank, UniCredit SpA. It states the bank intends to cut "around 8,000 jobs and 500 branches through 2023" and aims for "gross savings of €1 billion ($1.1 billion)". It also mentions the need to "retrain its staff to accomplish this" for new digital tools. As the speaker highlights these points, red underlines appear beneath "8,000 jobs", "500 branches", and "retrain its staff". The bottom left of the slide shows "Digital Science Center".

At 00:25, the slide changes to "Declining Physical Banks I". The man in the red polo shirt remains in the top right. The slide is divided into two charts. The left chart is a horizontal bar graph titled "UK Banks Closing The Biggest Share of Their Branches", showing percentages of branches closed by various banks between January 2015 and August 2019 (e.g., RBS 74%, Co-op 69%, Natwest 49%). The right chart is a vertical bar graph titled "Bank of America's Branch Network", showing a decrease in the number of branches from 5,976 in 2009 to 4,349 in 2019. A red diagonal line is drawn across the top of these bars, visually emphasizing the decline. The speaker notes this as about a "20% effect". "BUSINESS INSIDER INTELLIGENCE" and "Digital Science Center" are displayed at the bottom of the slide.

The video segment shows an older man with gray hair, wearing glasses and a red polo shirt, speaking directly to the camera from the top right corner of the screen. He occasionally gestures with his right hand. The main part of the screen displays a presentation slide titled "Declining Physical Banks I" against a white background. On the left side of the slide is a horizontal bar chart titled "UK Banks Closing The Biggest Share of Their Branches," showing percentages of branch closures for various UK banks between January 2015 and August 2019. RBS leads with 74% closures, while Lloyds closed 31%. A small note indicates "Banks with less than 30 closures not included" and the source "Which?, 2019". On the right side of the slide is a vertical bar chart titled "Bank of America's Branch Network," accompanied by the Bank of America logo. This chart illustrates a decline in Bank of America's branch network from 5,976 branches in 2009 to 4,349 in 2019, with a red line emphasizing the downward trend. The source for this data is "Company filings, The Wall Street Journal, 2018." Both charts feature the "BUSINESS INSIDER INTELLIGENCE" logo. At the bottom left of the slide, a blue bar contains the text "Digital Science Center." The speaker discusses the data presented on the slide, specifically mentioning the Royal Bank of Scotland's 74% closure rate and Lloyds' 31% closure rate. At the 0:25 mark, the video transitions to a new slide.

A man wearing glasses and a red polo shirt is visible in a small window at the bottom left of the screen, speaking to the camera while gesturing with his hands. Behind him is a plain white wall with a blurred abstract image. The main part of the screen displays a presentation slide titled "Declining Physical Banks II." On the left side of the slide, text reads "Business Inside Intelligence" and "BANKING PRO January 16, 2020," with "Digital Science Center" at the bottom left. The primary content of the slide is a graphic titled "Citibank's Digital Channels Grow As Physical Recedes Across three metrics," presenting three bar charts side-by-side. The first chart, "Online Banking Customer Growth Millions," shows increasing numbers of both "Mobile customers" (light gray bars, from 15.0 to 22.8 million) and "Digital customers" (dark gray bars, from 26.4 to 32.5 million) from Q4 2017 to Q4 2019. The second chart, "Agent Contact Rate," shows a decline from 1.34 in Q4 2017 to 1.26 in Q4 2019, annotated with a red arrow indicating a "-6%". The third chart, "E-Statement Penetration," shows an increase from 45% in Q4 2017 to 52% in Q4 2019, annotated with a red arrow indicating "+7 pct. pts.". As the man speaks, he points to the charts, with red drawn underlines highlighting "Mobile customers" and "Digital customers," and red drawn ellipses and arrows emphasizing the "Agent Contact Rate" decline and "E-Statement Penetration" increase. A note at the bottom of the graphic explains the "Agent contact rate" calculation and states the "Source: Company filings, 2020," with the "BUSINESS INSIDER INTELLIGENCE" logo at the bottom right.

In the video segment, a man in a red polo shirt is visible in the bottom right corner, actively speaking and gesturing. The main portion of the screen displays a white background with black text, headlined "AI and Size of Bank Staff" (AI and Size of Bank Staff). Below the title, an article dated "November 25, 2019" (November 25, 2019) is presented. The article describes Deutsche Bank's use of automation to achieve an 18,000-job cut target, noting a "massively increased productivity" (massively increased productivity) attributed to AI, machine learning tools, and bots. It details how these automated measures saved 680,000 hours of manual work and projects a 200,000-job reduction across the banking industry over the next decade. The speaker also comments that some of what is labeled "AI" (AI) is, in his view, "straightforward IT" (straightforward IT). A "Digital Science Center" (Digital Science Center) watermark is visible in the bottom left corner. The man's background includes a light-colored wall with what appears to be a framed picture or artwork.

The video segment opens with a white slide titled "AI and Size of Bank Staff," dated November 25, 2019. The main body of the text discusses Deutsche Bank's use of automation for job cuts, mentioning an 18,000-job target and a "massive 200,000-job reduction" across the banking industry over the next decade due to technology. Key phrases like "reports," "cited," "manual work," and "200,000-job" are highlighted in red. A man wearing a red polo shirt is visible in the bottom right corner, looking towards the screen and speaking, occasionally gesturing with his hands. At 0:32, the slide transitions to a new one titled "Making the Transition? Not everybody will," which cites an Economist article about Goldman Sachs' performance. This slide presents bullet points discussing the bank's past and present status, highlighting "declining profitability of capital-markets activity" and the "rising importance of technology in the industry," with the man in the red polo shirt continuing his presentation in the corner. Both slides feature "Digital Science Center" in the bottom left corner.

The video segment features a white slide with a black title, "Making the Transition? Not everybody will", presenting a detailed text from The Economist discussing Goldman Sachs' financial performance and the broader banking industry's struggles with technological transition, particularly with AI and digitalization. A red line underlines the source link and the phrase "technology in the industry" within the text. In the bottom right corner, a man with short white hair, wearing a red polo shirt, is visible in a small video inset, appearing to deliver a presentation. A white box in the bottom left reads "Digital Science Center". At 00:55, the slide changes to a new white one titled, "FINTECH WORKFORCE TO GROW BY 19% IN NEXT DECADE DUE TO AI While incumbents expect AI to reduce their headcount by 9%", which further elaborates on the impact of AI on the financial services workforce, highlighting differences between fintechs and incumbent banks. New red underlines appear on this slide below the "Digital Science Center" box and beneath "moving into finance" in the text, while the man in the red polo shirt continues to speak in the bottom right inset.

The video segment displays a screen primarily filled with a detailed text slide against a white background, while a man in a red short-sleeved shirt is visible in the bottom right corner. The slide's title reads: "FINTECH WORKFORCE TO GROW BY 19% IN NEXT DECADE DUE TO AI While incumbents expect AI to reduce their headcount by 9%". Below the title, bullet points summarize findings from a Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF) study. The man is speaking, gesturing slightly with his right hand, against a background featuring a colorful painting and a small potted plant. At 0:15, a red underline appears beneath "9%" in the title, and at 0:18, another red underline appears beneath "336,000" in the text, indicating the speaker's emphasis on these figures. The text further elaborates that incumbents expect a reduction of 336,000 jobs, while fintechs anticipate an increase of 37,000 jobs. A "Digital Science Center" logo is present in the bottom left corner of the screen.

The video displays a static image of text on a white background, covering most of the screen. The main title, "FINTECH WORKFORCE TO GROW BY 19% IN NEXT DECADE DUE TO AI While incumbents expect AI to reduce their headcount by 9%", is prominently displayed at the top. Below the title, several bullet points elaborate on the findings of a study by the Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF). Key phrases highlighted in red include "headcount by 9%" (underlined), "336,000" (underlined), and "37,000 jobs" (crossed out with a red line). The text discusses how AI is expected to reduce jobs in incumbent financial services by 336,000 while increasing jobs in fintechs by 37,000, attributing these trends to automation of back-office tasks by incumbents versus creation of new AI-based products by fintechs. In the bottom left corner, the text "Digital Science Center" is visible. On the bottom right, a man with short dark hair and glasses, wearing a red collared shirt, is seen from the chest up, speaking. He is gesturing slightly with his right hand as he talks. Behind him is a blurred background that appears to be an indoor setting with some faint colors and possibly a framed picture.

A man wearing a red collared shirt with short sleeves is visible in the bottom right corner of the frame, speaking and looking towards the camera. Behind him, a whiteboard with some writing and a potted plant are partially visible. The majority of the screen is dominated by a white presentation slide with black text. The main title reads: "FINTECH WORKFORCE TO GROW BY 19% IN NEXT DECADE DUE TO AI While incumbents expect AI to reduce their headcount by 9%". Below the title, several bullet points elaborate on this theme:
*   The first bullet mentions a "new study" (highlighted in blue, indicating a link) by the Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance (CCAF) at the University of Cambridge's Judge Business School. It states that "incumbents expect AI to reduce their headcount by 9% by 2030," while "fintechs expect the technology to expand their workforces by 19% in the next decade." It further specifies that this amounts to a "reduction of 336,000 jobs" (underlined in red) and an "increase of 37,000 jobs" (underlined in red) within the study's sample.
*   The second bullet attributes "incumbents' reduction" to "larger-scale automation of repetitive, labor-intensive back office tasks" (underlined in red). It also notes fintechs' increased focus on creating AI-based products and services.
*   The third bullet discusses how "fintechs" (highlighted in blue) may have a "leg up in the battle for tech talent," as both "incumbents" and "fintechs" (both highlighted in blue) struggle to attract and retain talent in the financial services industry as it "digitizes" (highlighted in blue). It suggests incumbents face "culture mismatches" with younger workers, while fintechs are appealing due to big tech companies "moving" (highlighted in blue) into finance.
At the bottom left of the screen, the text "Digital Science Center" is displayed on a blue background. The man continues to speak as the segment ends, with the slide remaining static.

The video features a man with short, graying hair, glasses, and a red short-sleeved collared shirt, seated in the bottom right corner, gesturing with his right hand while looking towards the screen. The main part of the screen displays a white presentation slide titled "Jobs Impact of AI in Banking," with a subtitle from "BUSINESS INSIDER Intelligence FINTECH PRO February 11, 2020". Below this, a bar chart titled "Financial Services Companies' Expected AI-Induced Net Job Changes, From 2019" illustrates "Absolute changes within the respondent sample." The chart shows stacked bars for the years 2022, 2025, and 2030, differentiating between "Incumbents" (light blue) and "Fintechs" (dark blue). For 2022, Incumbents show a 3% increase and Fintechs an 8% increase. For 2025, Incumbents show a -2% decrease and Fintechs a 10% increase. For 2030, Incumbents show a -9% decrease and Fintechs a 19% increase. A red underline appears beneath "2022" from 0:02 to 0:05. Subsequently, a red line graphs an upward trend for Fintechs from 2022 to 2030, starting at the top of the 2022 Fintech bar, passing over the 2025 Fintech bar, and ending above the 2030 Fintech bar (0:10-0:14). Another red line then graphs a downward trend for Incumbents from 2022 to 2030, starting at the top of the 2022 Incumbent bar, passing under the 2025 Incumbent bar, and ending below the 2030 Incumbent bar (0:16-0:24). The bottom left of the slide has a "Digital Science Center" logo, and the bottom right features the "BUSINESS INSIDER INTELLIGENCE" logo, with the source "Cambridge Centre for Alternative Finance, 2020, n=151" at the bottom left. The man's background consists of a wall adorned with a large image or tapestry depicting yellow flowers, possibly sunflowers, and green leaves.
